title: operant TUI headless visual-regression scenario corpus (v1)
description: Contract for the Phase 0 `--suite` runner. One `*.scenario.json` file per renderable TUI surface. The runner renders each scenario headlessly via ratatui's TestBackend (TuiApp::run_headless), writes a text dump and a style dump, and diffs both against the committed baselines named here. Every field below was cross-checked against the real implementation: `assert` paths against App::debug_snapshot()/overlay_flags() in crates/operant-cli/src/tui/app/commands.rs, `keys` tokens against parse_key_sequence() in crates/operant-cli/src/cmd_tui_debug.rs, and `agent_script` event shapes against MockAgentEvent in the same file.

notes: The runner MUST only pick up files matching `*.scenario.json`; any other file in this directory (README.md, tooling, this schema) is ignored.
`baselines/` is created by Phase 0 on first `--update-baselines` run; the corpus only names the files.
Two baselines per scenario: `<baseline>` (text) and `<style_baseline>` (style grid).

`excluded.json` is the single source of truth for surfaces the corpus tracks but does not execute. Each entry names the surface, the baselines a future run should create, one `reason`, and an `unblock_when`. It is NOT a pass list: the runner prints its size so a run can never quietly shrink its own regression net, and _validate.py cross-checks it against the SURFACES ledger so an entry can never drift out of sync with the render ladder.

name.meaning: Unique kebab-case id; also the primary key the runner keys baselines on and the name it prints in CI.
name.notes: Must be unique across the directory. Renaming a scenario orphans its baselines — treat as a breaking change.

surface.meaning: The source path or `module::fn` that renders this surface.
surface.notes: Points at the render function, not the state struct, so a refactor that moves a renderer shows up as a one-line diff here. Use `<file>::<fn>` for `render_*` functions and a bare `<file>` for state-only surfaces.

opens_with.meaning: The slash command or key chord that opens the surface, in human form (`/help`, `Ctrl+R`).
opens_with.notes: Documentation only — the machine-readable opener is `keys`. Listed separately so a reader can grep openers without parsing key syntax.

keys.meaning: Full key sequence for the scenario, INCLUDING the opener and any closing keys, in `--keys` syntax.
keys.notes: See `key_syntax`. An empty string is legal and means 'render the landing frame with zero keystrokes'.

flags.meaning: Extra CLI flags appended verbatim to the `simulate` invocation, for state that cannot be produced by a key or an agent-script event.
flags.notes: Currently only `--bypass-permissions` is used. That one is a flag rather than a script event because `TuiApp::enter` raises the dialog before any key or event is processed, and it mirrors the real `operant --dangerously-skip-permissions`. The runner MUST NOT invent or infer flags; anything here is echoed into the command line.

size.meaning: Terminal size as WxH passed to `--size`.
size.notes: Default corpus size is 120x40. `run_headless` clamps to at least 20x5 via `width.max(20)` / `height.max(5)`, so values below that are silently altered — do not use them. Narrow/short coverage belongs in `variants`, not here.

size.meaning: Alternate terminal size for this scenario.

keys.meaning: Alternate key sequence; defaults to the scenario's `keys` when omitted.

assert.meaning: State assertions applied INSTEAD OF the scenario's `assert` for this variant.

assert_screen.meaning: Screen assertions applied INSTEAD OF the scenario's `assert_screen` for this variant.

items.meaning: Extra renders of the same surface at other geometries, for narrow/short-terminal layout regressions. Each variant gets its OWN pair of baselines, named `<baseline stem>.<W>x<H>.txt` / `.style.txt`.

agent_script.notes: Omit for surfaces that need no agent output. Setting it flips `run_headless` onto the mock path: no network, no models.dev fetch. Every script MUST end in a `done` or `error` event — see `agent_script_contract`.

assert.meaning: State assertions joined with `,` and passed to `--assert`.
assert.notes: See `assertion_syntax`. At least one entry MUST prove the surface actually opened — not merely that a key was accepted. An unresolvable path is a HARD FAILURE of the run (evaluate_assertions bails with "Unknown assertion path"), so a typo here silently removes the surface from coverage.

assert_screen.meaning: Screen assertions joined with `,` and passed to `--assert-screen`.
assert_screen.notes: See `screen_assertion_syntax`. Matched against `screen.join("\n")` where each row is `trim_end()`-ed. Comma is the clause separator, so a needle containing a literal comma must be avoided or the clause will be split.

baseline.meaning: Filename under `baselines/` holding the text dump for this scenario.

style_baseline.meaning: Filename under `baselines/` holding the per-cell style dump for this scenario.
style_baseline.notes: See `baseline_formats.style`. This is what catches a colour regression, which the text dump cannot.

notes.meaning: Why this scenario exists / what regression it catches.

reachability.meaning: `live` = executes green against the real binary today. `blocked` = the surface is rendered by render_app but cannot be reached through `parse_key_sequence`'s current token set or the headless driver; the scenario states exactly what Phase 0 must change.
reachability.notes: Phase 0's runner MUST report `blocked` scenarios as SKIPPED-with-reason rather than as failures, and MUST print the `blocked_by` text, so an unreachable surface never reads as a passing surface.

blocked_by.meaning: Required only when `reachability == "blocked"`. One sentence naming the exact missing capability and where it would have to be added.
blocked_by.notes: Each of these names a concrete, small change: a new token in parse_key_sequence, a flag on TuiApp::enter, or a new event channel in run_headless.

key_syntax.grammar: A --keys string is a flat char stream. Everything not matched below is emitted as a literal KeyCode::Char.

generic_grammars.function_keys: <f1> .. <f12> -> KeyCode::F(n). Digits only and 1..=12 only, so `<f0>` and `<f13>` stay unrecognised instead of wrapping.
generic_grammars.modifier_chords: <ctrl+<c>> / <alt+<c>> / any `+`-joined combination of ctrl|control|alt|meta|option|shift, ending in a single character. At least one modifier is required. Case-insensitive: `<CTRL+K>` == `<ctrl+k>`. Examples: <ctrl+k>, <alt+v>, <ctrl+shift+m>, <ctrl+alt+p>.

key_syntax.unrecognised_bracketed_token: FALLS THROUGH AS LITERAL CHARACTERS. parse_key_sequence sets parsed=false and then emits '<', then each inner char, then '>'. There is no error. `<f13>` therefore types the six characters `<f13>`; it does NOT press F13. This is the single largest footgun in the corpus and it is deliberately preserved: a scenario naming a binding the parser does not know must show up as typed text, never as a silent no-op.
key_syntax.notes: Slash commands are typed literally: `/help<enter>` is 5 chars + Enter = 6 key events.

assertion_syntax.contains_delimiter: ' contains ' — the operator must be surrounded by spaces, otherwise it is not recognised and the clause is a parse error.
assertion_syntax.value_quoting: Outer matching single or double quotes are stripped from the value. Omit them unless the value itself needs them.
assertion_syntax.legacy_alias: A path ending in `.visible` is rewritten to `overlays.<base>`. `help_overlay.visible == true` and `overlays.help_overlay == true` are equivalent; the corpus uses the canonical form.
assertion_syntax.type_coercion: Booleans and numbers are parsed from the value string and compared to the JSON node; strings compare by equality; `contains` does a substring test against the node's display form. `status_message` is `null` when unset, so `status_message contains x` FAILS on a null node — use `==` for presence checks.

top_level_paths.focus: string (Debug of the Focus enum, e.g. "Input", "Prompt", "None")
top_level_paths.overlays: object of 34 booleans — the ONLY place a dialog/overlay visibility can be asserted

not_in_snapshot: usage_overlay — rendered by render_app (F8) but absent from overlay_flags(), so `overlays.usage_overlay` FAILS with "Unknown assertion path"
debug_hub / debug overlay — rendered by render_app (F12) but absent from overlay_flags()
tool_use_blocks, context_menu_state, selection_anchor/focus, notifications, streaming_text, system_annotations, background_tasks — none are exposed by debug_snapshot()

screen_assertion_syntax.row_production: Each buffer row is the concatenation of cell symbols, then trim_end(). Trailing spaces are therefore absent; a needle must not rely on them. Wide/combining glyphs appear as the raw symbol string.
screen_assertion_syntax.comma_caveat: evaluate_screen_assertions splits on ','. A needle containing a comma cannot be expressed.
screen_assertion_syntax.notes: Screen assertions are the ONLY way to verify a surface that debug_snapshot() does not expose (footer, typeahead, transcript text, tool blocks).

agent_script_contract.format: A JSON array of objects tagged by `type` (serde `rename_all = "snake_case"`).

user.notes: NOT an AgentEvent. `build_transcript_turns` starts a new turn only at a `Role::User` message, and `render_messages` partitions tool blocks onto a turn — so a script with tool events and no `user` event populates tool state and paints no tool block. Lead the script with `user` whenever it contains tool_* events.

permission_request.notes: NOT an AgentEvent. Sends on the same bounded channel `agent.with_permissions(permission_tx)` writes to, which `App::run` drains into the `permission_request` dialog. Raises `overlays.permission_request`.

user_question.notes: NOT an AgentEvent. Sends on the unbounded channel the `clarify` tool writes to (registered globally via `set_user_question_sender`), which `App::run` drains into `ask_user_dialog`. Omit `choices` for the free-text form.

background_task.notes: NOT an AgentEvent. Calls operant_core's public `create_record` / `mark_completed` / `mark_failed` — the same process-wide registry `SubAgentTool::dispatch_background` writes and that `BackgroundTaskState::refresh` reads. `status` is one of `pending`, `completed`, `failed`. The rendered row is derived from that record, never injected into TUI state.

usage.notes: total_tokens is computed as the sum; do not supply it.

done.notes: Terminal for a normal turn. DO NOT follow an `error` with a `done`: `handle_agent_event` auto-dismisses error notifications on the next Content/Thinking/Reasoning/Done, and the real agent never emits Done after Error (both `AgentEvent::Error` sites in operant-core/src/agent/run.rs return Err immediately). An error-then-done script silently swallows the error modal.

error.notes: Terminal. Raises an `Error:` transcript line AND an Error notification, which is what puts the error modal on screen.

agent_script_contract.unknown_field: Rejected by serde (the enum is not `deny_unknown_fields`-tolerant by default); an unrecognised key fails the whole script parse with "Failed to parse agent script".
agent_script_contract.termination: MUST end in `done` or `error`. run_headless pre-resolves the run_complete oneshot so the loop terminates regardless, but a script with no terminal event leaves the transcript mid-turn and the run reads like a hang.
known_limitations: tool_start/tool_complete/tool_error only paint a tool block if the script leads with a `user` event — see the `user` variant above.
`error` paints the error modal only while it is the LAST event; see `done` above.

The `mcp_approval` dialog cannot be produced by any script, because `McpApprovalDialogState::show` has no call site anywhere in the workspace (it is `#[allow(dead_code)]`). That is a product gap, not a harness one — see excluded.json.
`apply_selection_highlight` cannot be produced: its only state writer is the mouse handler, and `App::run` drives a `Vec<KeyEvent>` with no mouse source. See excluded.json.

Setting agent_script sets is_mock, which SKIPS load_models_dev(). The model picker's list is therefore empty on the mock path — a model-picker scenario that wants a populated list must run without an agent_script and accept the network dependency.

library_entries.assistant-simple.json: One Content + Done. The minimal healthy transcript.
library_entries.usage.json: Content + Usage + Done. The only way to get non-zero token glyphs in the footer without a network turn.
library_entries.stream-multi-chunk.json: Two Reasoning events then three Content events. Exercises the thinking row and proves the stream coalesces into one message.
library_entries.reasoning-then-answer.json: Thinking + Reasoning + Content + Done(reasoning). Pairs with stream-multi-chunk to cover both mock event variants of the same render path.
library_entries.tool-error.json: User + Content + ToolStart + ToolError + Done. Proves the failure text survives into the flushed assistant message.
library_entries.tool-run-completed.json: User + Content + ToolStart + ToolComplete + Done. The `user` event is what makes the tool block paint; it is the tool-block scenario's script.
library_entries.error-modal.json: Thinking + Content + Error, and NOTHING after. The error-modal scenario's script: a trailing `done` would auto-dismiss the modal it is meant to show.
library_entries.permission-request.json: User + permission_request + Done. Raises the permission dialog through the real `permission_rx` channel.
library_entries.ask-user-question.json: User + user_question + Done. Raises the ask-user dialog through the real user-question channel.
library_entries.background-task.json: Two background_task records (one pending, one completed) + Done. Produces the two background-task rows plus the footer count.
library_entries.empty.json: A single Done and nothing else. Reserved as the runner's own minimal-termination fixture — deliberately NOT referenced by any scenario, because its job is to prove a one-event script still flips is_streaming and ends the loop, which is a harness property rather than a surface.

text.encoding: UTF-8, LF line endings, single trailing newline
text.content: The exact bytes `--dump-screen` writes today: `screen.join("\n")`, i.e. one row per line, no trailing newline beyond the final row's own terminator.
text.row_definition: For y in 0..height: concatenate buf.content()[y*width .. (y+1)*width] cell symbols, then trim_end().
text.row_count: Exactly `height` rows — trailing all-blank rows are KEPT (they are trimmed of trailing spaces but not dropped). A row count change is itself a regression signal.
text.diff: Line-by-line. Report the first differing row index, both rows, and the 0-based column of the first differing character.
text.known_nondeterminism: Rows that embed wall-clock time, absolute paths, git output, session/skill/plugin listings, model ids, or `~/.operant/slash-usage.json`-driven ordering differ per machine. Scenarios whose surface reads those carry an `env_requirements` note; the runner should either mask them or keep such baselines out of the blocking set.

style.encoding: UTF-8, LF line endings, single trailing newline
style.purpose: Catches colour and modifier regressions, which the text dump cannot see. Two surfaces can render identical text with inverted palettes; only this file notices.
style.layout: A header line, then exactly `height` grid lines of exactly `width` tokens, space-separated.
style.symbol_field: The cell symbol with these substitutions, so a style file stays one-token-per-cell and diff-friendly: space -> `_`; empty symbol or NUL -> `~`; backslash -> `\\`; any other control char -> `?`; a cell whose symbol is wider than 1 column (wide CJK/emoji) is written once, in the cell where it STARTS, and its continuation cells are written as `~/<same fg>/<same bg>/-`. Every other printable char is written literally.
style.bg_field: Same vocabulary as fg. An unset background is written as `-`; `Color::Reset` background is written as `reset`.
style.mods_field: A `-`-joined, alphabetically sorted, `+`-separated subset of `b`(bold) `i`(italic) `u`(underline) `r`(reversed) `d`(dim) `x`(crossedout); the literal `-` when no modifier is set. A style with fg=X, bg=-, no modifiers encodes as `X/-/-@_`.
style.example_line: cyan/-/b-@█ and -/darkgray/-@_ are both valid tokens for that row.
style.diff: Token-by-token on the grid, plus a whole-line check on the header. Report the first differing (row, col) and both tokens.
style.normalisation: The writer MUST NOT normalise or reorder anything; the dump is a verbatim projection of the TestBackend buffer so any post-processing would hide exactly the regressions this file exists to catch.

phase_0_flags_to_add: --dump-style <path> — write the style baseline described above
--baseline <path> — write the text baseline described above
determinism_requirements: Never run two scenarios concurrently in one process: the mock path and slash-command handling touch process-wide state (slash usage store, notification and background-task registries, audio detection).
Freeze or record the clock. Several surfaces embed elapsed time (footer turn timer, session-start-seeded tips).
Pin HOME (or OPERANT_HOME) to a fixture directory seeded with skills/plugins/auth so `/skills`, `/plugins` and `/model` render the same rows on every machine.
Set the terminal size explicitly per scenario; never inherit the developer's tty.

conventions.naming: scenario file = `<name>.scenario.json`; baselines = `<name>.txt` and `<name>.style.txt`; variants append `.<W>x<H>` before the extension.
conventions.env_requirements: Recorded in `notes` as a leading `ENV:` clause when a scenario reads machine state. The runner may parse it to decide whether to run the scenario in a blocking or advisory tier.
conventions.assertion_style: One assertion per surface is a common failure mode — `any_modal_open == true` alone would pass for 29 different overlays. Every scenario asserts its OWN `overlays.<name> == true`. Two further rules learned the hard way: (1) assert a surface's OWN text, not a proxy — `any_modal_open == false` proves nothing about whether a surface rendered, and the two non-modal panels (usage_overlay, debug_overlay) are exposed as TOP-LEVEL snapshot keys precisely because folding them into overlay_flags() would make any_modal_open lie. (2) a needle may not contain a comma: evaluate_screen_assertions splits clauses on ','. `contains:► [y] Yes, allow once` silently becomes two clauses — stop the needle at the last comma-free word.
conventions.any_modal_open_is_host_dependent: any_modal_open ORs all 34 overlay flags plus show_help and context_menu_state. On a host with a working audio device, TuiApp::enter calls voice_mode_notice.show_if_available(..) and the notice is visible from frame 0, so any_modal_open is TRUE for the entire run. An `any_modal_open == false` assertion is therefore only meaningful on a host where the boot notice did not appear — use a leading `/voice<enter>` (which replaces the notice with a fresh invisible state) when a scenario genuinely needs no modal open, as `notification-banner` does. An `any_modal_open == true` assertion, by contrast, is always safe.
conventions.blocked_scenario_policy: `reachability: "blocked"` is a TEMPORARY marker for a surface that will be unblocked in this iteration; the runner prints `blocked_by` and counts it as SKIPPED. A surface that cannot be made reachable belongs in `excluded.json` instead, not here — a scenario file that cannot pass teaches people to ignore red. The corpus currently has zero blocked entries; anything marked blocked makes _validate.py warn.
conventions.host_dependent_startup_state: On a host with a working audio device, TuiApp::enter calls `voice_mode_notice.show_if_available(..)`, so voice_mode_notice is visible from frame 0 and `any_modal_open` is TRUE before any key is pressed. A scenario that needs a clean start must lead with `/voice<enter>`, which replaces the notice with a fresh invisible state and is idempotent on a silent host. `<esc>` also works, EXCEPT when an Error notification is current: Esc then hits `dismiss_error_notifications()` and takes the modal down with it. The error-modal scenario therefore sends no keys at all and does not assert any_modal_open.

authoring_tools._validate.py: Static corpus checker. Encodes the ground truth (the 15 debug_snapshot top-level keys, the 34 overlay_flags keys, the parse_key_sequence token table, the MockAgentEvent variant table) and fails on: unparseable JSON, missing/mistyped fields, a key token the parser does not recognise, an assert path that does not resolve, a screen clause that is not contains:/not-contains:, a needle containing the ',' clause separator, a missing or malformed agent script, a script that does not end in done/error, and any surface with no scenario.
authoring_tools._run.py: Prototype Phase 0 runner. Executes every `live` scenario and every variant using ONLY flags that exist today — --keys, --size, --assert, --assert-screen, --agent-script, --dump-screen. Never uses --dump-style or --baseline, which Phase 0 must add.
